All Phillies players will get paid a bonus for the Field of Dreams Game

August 13, 2026 | 12:35 PM EDT
Tim Kelly

A Decrease font size. A Reset font size. A Increase font size.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:42
Instaread

DYERSVILLE, Iowa — Phillies and Minnesota Twins players will get paid extra for participating in the 2026 MLB Field of Dreams Game.

According to Matt Gelb of The Athletic, it has been collectively bargained that all 27 players on the active roster for the one-off game will get paid an extra stipend:

“The Phillies and Twins are each permitted an extra player for the game, but it cannot be a pitcher. As collectively bargained between the league and players’ union, every player on the active roster for the Iowa game receives a $20,000 payment.”

Obviously, the Phillies have a veteran-heavy team with many players who have made tens, if not hundreds, of millions in their careers. To them, $20,000 is like pocket change. However, to some of the younger players on the roster, that’s a nice chunk of change. Whatever position player the Phillies call up for the game to be the 27th man stands to benefit the most, particularly since they aren’t guaranteed to play and will almost certainly be returned to Triple-A after the game.

MLB and the MLBPA have funds set aside for things like this that both parties believe are good for the game, but an inconvenience to players during a 162-game season. Another example of this is that Andrew Marchand reported in The New York Post years ago that players get paid $10,000 to do in-game interviews on national broadcasts. (We can debate whether in-game interviews are actually good for the game, but MLB thinks so and the MLBPA isn’t going to turn down the chance to get players an extra $10,000.)

In this case, players might be further inconvenienced by weather that could turn Thursday into a very long night and/or force the game to be postponed until Friday, erasing what is supposed to be a scheduled travel day before the series resumes at Target Field in Minneapolis on Saturday.
